approach: Three changes meet in the throughput review. (1) athena-data: a `WasteFigures` struct (attempts per landing, wasted USD, first-attempt share), an optional defaulted `waste` field on `ThroughputReview`, and a `Wasted` trigger, so old records still parse. (2) status.rs: `waste_windows(records, window)` returns the newest window (partial allowed, with its landing count) and up to three full windows before it. `Throughput::compute` keeps the newest window, the one before it, the median for both, and per measure a noise estimate and a one-job resolution floor. `Throughput::text()` prints the three measures, so `athena status` shows them. (3) hestia.rs: `throughput_due` fires `Wasted` on a rise of more than 20% against the figures stored on the previous review. `throughput_review` never skips for an open design request: it names the request in the record's note and in THROUGHPUT.md, and it always asks the model on a due review. A pure `request_gate` decides whether a design request is queued. Judged case (at least 60 landings): queue only when a measure got worse by MORE than max(noise, floor), newest full 20-landing window vs the 20 before. Noise is the largest adjacent difference among the older full windows. Not-judged case (under 60 landings): no design request, except the very first review when none is open. NEW this round: the slowdown request (25% rule) also goes through the noise rule on the median measure when noise can be estimated (60+ landings): it is queued only if the rise over the previous review's median also exceeds max(median noise, 1 minute). Under 60 landings noise cannot be estimated, the 25% rule alone applies as today, and the note says so. All notes say which kind of request they speak about. The shared `did_not_land(job)` helper keeps the no-invocations guard inside it. The steady-trend blind spot of adjacent-difference noise is named in hestia.md and the risks. No parser, stem list or reading rule changes, so refusal_corpus is not touched.

decisions.choice: 1. Definitions. Landing = a landed request job. Attempt in a window = its landings + its did-not-land attempts. A did-not-land attempt is a request job WITH invocations that failed, was closed unlanded, or was stopped. The predicate is moved into a shared helper `did_not_land(job) -> bool` that INCLUDES the guard `if job.invocations.is_empty() { return false }` (today that guard is the `continue` at status.rs:1011-1013, before the check at 1015-1018), so a closed unlanded job that never ran is not counted. The loop in `Throughput::compute` calls the helper after still handling `busy_intervals` for jobs with invocations, with unchanged results. Jobs still open count in neither side until they close. First-attempt landing = a landed job whose request is not 'try again on <job>' pointing at an earlier job that did work (`reading::retried_job`, reading.rs:1522). Wasted spend = `JobRecords::spent_usd` (store.rs:169) summed over the window's did-not-land attempts.
decisions.reason: All figures come from job and invocation records, so no new record type is needed. Leaving open jobs out means attempts per landing is not inflated by work in flight, and every counted attempt has a close time to place it in a window. The guard inside the helper (answers finding 4) keeps requests that closed before any run from inflating attempts per landing. The retry link is the codebase's existing meaning of 'another attempt at the same change'.

rejected.option: Count every request job with invocations as an attempt
rejected.why: A running or waiting job is neither a landing nor wasted, which inflates attempts per landing and gives it no window.

rejected.option: Helper made only from lines 1015-1018 without the empty-invocations guard
rejected.why: It would count closed unlanded jobs that never ran as attempts and inflate attempts per landing.

rejected.option: Read cost from Outcome.totals.cost_all
rejected.why: Jobs stopped before an outcome carry no totals.

rejected.option: Count invocations or producer runs as attempts
rejected.why: A job's planner, critic and verifier runs are not attempts to land a change; the request's '58% of attempts did not land' is about jobs.

decisions.choice: 2. Windows. Landed request jobs are ranked by (landing end, id), the ranking `landed_jobs_among_first` uses (status.rs:963), shared as a helper. Window 0 = the newest 20 landings (all when fewer) plus every did-not-land attempt that closed at or after the oldest of those landings' end. Windows 1-3 = landings 21-40, 41-60, 61-80 plus did-not-land attempts closed between their cut times. An attempt is placed by its closing outcome time, or its last invocation end if it has none. Window 0 is reported even when partial, with its landing count printed (status.rs:1003 uses saturating_sub for the median section). Windows 1-3 are reported only when full. `waste_windows(records, window)` takes the size so tests can use small windows; production passes THROUGHPUT_WINDOW. The median windows use the same cut over the measured jobs of `landed_jobs`. Each window keeps the cost of each of its did-not-land attempts (private Vec) for the spend floor.
decisions.reason: `athena status` and the first review show the three measures with fewer than 20 landings (the one-landing snapshot fixture shows 1.00, 0.00 USD, 100%). A thin window can never be the 'previous' window, so it cannot gate anything. The cut by landing end avoids a second time axis.

rejected.option: Report only full windows
rejected.why: Hides the measures in any repository under 20 landings and breaks the criterion 5 fixture, which has one landing.

rejected.option: Windows cut by calendar time
rejected.why: Landings per day vary, so a window would not be 20 changes.

rejected.option: Waste figures over the measured jobs of landed_jobs() only
rejected.why: It drops landed jobs that ran no model, which are still landings.

decisions.choice: 3. Trigger `throughput_due(landed, median, waste: Option<WasteFigures>, latest)` compares the newest-window figures with the figures stored on the previous review (new `waste: Option<WasteFigures>`), as the median trigger uses `window_median_minutes`, and needs a landing since that review. Rises: attempts per landing > previous x WORSEN_RATIO; wasted USD > previous x WORSEN_RATIO; first-attempt share < previous x (2 - WORSEN_RATIO). Zero floor: when the previous wasted USD is 0, the spend rise counts only if attempts per landing also exceeds previous x WORSEN_RATIO. A previous review with no stored figures gives no waste trigger. Cadence still fires first at 10 landings beyond the previous review. The trigger only decides that a review runs; the gate (decision 4) decides whether a design request is queued.
decisions.reason: A level that stays high triggers once, not on every landing, and old records stay valid. The zero floor ties a rise from zero to a measured ratio, not to a fixed cent value.

rejected.option: Trigger on newest 20 vs the 20 before, recomputed
rejected.why: A level that stays high would fire on every new landing.

rejected.option: Any wasted spend of 0.01 USD or more after a zero baseline
rejected.why: One failed run after a clean window would fire a review.

rejected.option: One ThroughputTrigger variant per measure
rejected.why: One `Wasted` variant suffices; the note names the measures that rose.

decisions.choice: 4. The design-request gate. `request_gate` is pure and decides only whether a DESIGN request is queued; the model is asked on every due review. For each of four measures (median minutes, attempts per landing, wasted USD, first-attempt share), when windows 0, 1 and 2 are full (60 landings): change = window 0 minus window 1 in the bad direction. Noise = the largest adjacent difference among the older full windows, |w1-w2| and |w2-w3| when window 3 is full. Floor = the smallest change one job can make: 1/window for attempts per landing and for share; for spend the median cost of one did-not-land attempt pooled over full windows 0-2 (and 3 when full), 0 when none; 1 minute for the median. Beyond noise only when change > max(noise, floor); equal is within. A measure whose own windows are not full is left out and the note says so. Judged: queue iff at least one measure is beyond; the note starts 'design request:' and names each beyond measure with change, noise, floor and the number of differences used (1 or 2), or says 'within noise' (naming the larger bound) or 'no measure worsened'. Not judged (under 60 landings): queue nothing and write 'design request: not enough history: N of 60 landings, none queued', except the first review (no earlier review), which queues when no throughput design request is open, as today. hestia.md and the note name the blind spot: noise taken from adjacent differences absorbs a steady trend, so a steady, equal-step worsening (for example spend 2, 4, 6, then 8) is within noise and queues nothing; the 20% trigger and cadence still run the review and the model's proposal is still recorded.
decisions.reason: Change and noise are both differences between non-overlapping 20-landing windows, so they are like for like, and the newest pair is excluded from its own noise. Floors stop a flat older history (noise 0) from turning one retried landing or one failed run into a request. 'Cannot judge' means 'do not queue' so a young repository gets no request on every review, while the model is still asked so a due review never does nothing. Finding 3 of this round: the blind spot is accepted and documented because the accepted reading defines noise as the spread between recent windows.

rejected.option: Noise from differences around the older windows' mean (detrended)
rejected.why: With 2 or 3 older windows the mean fit leaves one degree of freedom or none, so it is less stable than adjacent differences and harder to state in a note; the blind spot is documented instead.

rejected.option: Noise alone as the bar
rejected.why: A flat older history gives noise 0, so any worsening queues a request.

rejected.option: A fixed percentage threshold
rejected.why: It is the 20% trigger again and does not adapt to the repository.

rejected.option: Floor for spend as a fixed cent value
rejected.why: Arbitrary; the median cost of one did-not-land attempt is measured.

rejected.option: Cannot judge means queue
rejected.why: With the skip removed it queues a design request on every due review below 60 landings.

rejected.option: Skip the model whenever the gate rejects
rejected.why: Most cadence reviews would do nothing, the complaint behind the request.

rejected.option: Change = current vs the previous review's stored figures
rejected.why: That review may be 1 to 9 landings old, so its window overlaps window 0 and the change is diluted against a non-overlapping noise.

decisions.choice: 5. An open earlier design request no longer stops the review. The record's note says 'throughput design request <id> is still open; this review ran anyway', THROUGHPUT.md names the open request (id and title) so the proposal differs from it, the model is asked, and the proposal is recorded. A design request is queued only if the gate says so. When a request is open and the gate says queue, a second one is queued; both are linked by their reviews' `proposal.request_job`. When the gate says no, the proposal is recorded with `request_job: None` (as in the existing 'could not be queued' path).
decisions.reason: This is 'does not skip a run' plus 'notes the open request' plus 'only queues beyond noise'. No code assumes at most one throughput design request: `improvement_of` (hestia.rs:409-443) returns a set and `Plan::build_improving` (plan.rs:832-839) treats it as a set.

rejected.option: Keep the skip and reword it
rejected.why: The request calls the skipped runs 'did nothing'.

rejected.option: Ask the model but never queue while a request is open
rejected.why: A change beyond noise would go unanswered until the open request closes; left as open question 1.

decisions.choice: 6. Existing hestia tests are rewritten exactly where the new behaviour changes their assertions. Rewritten: (a) `a_review_queues_one_design_request_...` (4411), second review: assert `proposal` is Some with `request_job == None`, the note holds 'still open', `open_design_requests` stays 1, the model log has 2 entries. (b) `a_median_rise_from_25_to_60_...` (4628): first half asserts proposal Some with `request_job None`, model log 1, one open design request, and the unchanged slowdown assertions (21 landings, so noise is not estimable and the 25% rule alone applies); second half asserts model log 2 and open design requests stay 1. (c) `unmeasured_landed_jobs_before_...` (4724): model log has 1 entry (was empty). (d) `a_flat_median_queues_nothing` (4757): model log has 1 entry, no request queued, nothing reported. (e) The 4790 test, the improvement_of test (5116) and the followup tests at 4526 and 4561 need no assertion change; every seed_landed call in them stays under 60 landings (lines 4390-5142 read), so the slowdown noise rule never applies to them. `Lines` and the `earlier_review` literal get the new field.
decisions.reason: The dependents list matches what decisions 4, 5 and 8 do, test by test.

rejected.option: State that 4411 and 4757 pass unchanged
rejected.why: They assert the model is not called; under always-ask the log has more entries.

decisions.choice: 7. display.rs and snapshot.rs are not edited. Both print `Throughput::text()` (display.rs:1114 and :1203, snapshot.rs:245/276) and snapshot.rs serializes the `Throughput` struct, so new fields and lines flow through. The status_snapshot test is extended to assert the new labels.
decisions.reason: A separate renderer would duplicate text() and could drift from what the review is given. The brief lists both as expected deliverables, but a file with no needed change stays untouched ('small').

rejected.option: Separate display code for the three measures
rejected.why: It would duplicate text() and could drift.

decisions.choice: 8. The slowdown request (answers finding 1, option (a)). `compare_with_previous_review` (hestia.rs:1839-1902) keeps its 25% rule (`is_slowdown`, hestia.rs:1475) and the stage-growth condition, and adds one condition: when `measured.bars.median.noise` is Some (windows 0-2 of the median are full, 60 landings), the slowdown request is queued only if the rise (current median minus the previous review's `window_median_minutes`) is MORE than max(median noise, 1 minute floor). Otherwise a remark says 'slowdown request: median rose X to Y, within noise (noise N, floor F, D differences); none queued'. When noise is None (under 60 landings) the 25% rule alone decides, as today, and the remark says 'noise could not be estimated (N of 60 landings); the 25% rule applied'. The check is a small pure function `slowdown_beyond_noise(rise, bar) -> Result<(), String>` called inside the `Some(grown)` arm before the open-slowdown and queue steps. Every note says which kind of request it speaks about ('design request:' or 'slowdown request:'), so the criterion 3 note ('design request: not enough history ... none queued' plus 'slowdown request ... queued at high priority ... noise could not be estimated') agrees with what the review did. docs/design/hestia.md and CHANGELOG state this.
decisions.reason: The request says the review 'only queues a request when the change is larger than the noise between recent windows'. The slowdown request is a request the review queues, so it follows the noise rule wherever noise exists. Where noise cannot be estimated the existing, tested 25% rule keeps working, so no existing slowdown test changes. Out-of-scope forbids changing the 25% rule beyond what the noise rule needs; the added condition is only the noise rule.

rejected.option: (b) Leave the slowdown ungated and word the note for design requests only
rejected.why: It leaves a request path that ignores noise, against the accepted reading.

rejected.option: Gate the slowdown the same way as design requests (nothing under 60 landings)
rejected.why: It would silence the slowdown request in every young repository and break the 4628 test, a change beyond what the noise rule needs.

rejected.option: Use the window-0-vs-window-1 change instead of the rise over the previous review
rejected.why: The slowdown rule compares with the previous review (its own basis); changing the basis would change the 25% rule.

Add `did_not_land` (guard included), the shared landing ranking helper, `WasteWindow` (with per-attempt costs), `waste_windows`, the median windows, noise and floors per measure, the new `Throughput` fields, the three printed measures with basis lines in `text()`, and tests for criteria 1 and 5.

Extend `throughput_due`; add `waste_rises`, `request_gate` and `slowdown_beyond_noise`; change `throughput_review` so an open request is noted not skipped, the model is always asked, the gate decides design-request queuing, and the record stores the figures; add the noise condition to the slowdown arm of `compare_with_previous_review`; name the open request in THROUGHPUT.md via `ask_throughput`; update docs; add helpers and tests; rewrite the existing tests listed in decision 6.

risks.risk: Every due review now calls the model, including those that queue nothing, so model spend per due review is no longer capped by an open request.
risks.mitigation: This matches today's cost when no request is open; reviews are due only on a 10-landing cadence or a rise; the record keeps the invocation; open question 3 asks the user.

risks.risk: Under 60 landings no design request is queued after the first review, so a young repository gets fewer design requests than today.
risks.mitigation: The note says 'not enough history: N of 60 landings'; the model's proposal is still recorded; CHANGELOG and hestia.md state the rule; open question 2 asks the user.

risks.risk: The noise rests on one difference with exactly 60 landings, so the gate can swing from run to run.
risks.mitigation: The note states the number of differences used (1 or 2) next to the noise; the one-job floor bounds the swing from below.

risks.risk: Blind spot: noise from adjacent differences absorbs a steady trend, so an equal-step worsening (spend 2, 4, 6, then 8) is within noise and queues no design request.
risks.mitigation: Named in hestia.md and in the CHANGELOG; the 20% trigger and the cadence still run the review and the model's proposal is still recorded; the 25% slowdown rule is a separate path for the median.

risks.risk: Two or three failed runs after a clean history exceed the one-job floor and queue a request.
risks.mitigation: That is more than one job's worth in a 20-landing window and is stated in the note and hestia.md; the 20% trigger and cadence decide whether a review runs, the floor only whether it queues; open question 4 asks about the floor values.

risks.risk: Two design requests can be open at once and both get the guaranteed turn.
risks.mitigation: A second is queued only beyond the bar; THROUGHPUT.md names the open request so the proposal differs; the criterion 4 test asserts `improvement_of` lists both; build_improving is set-based.

risks.risk: Failed-job fixtures end in the wrong window, so the criterion 1, 2(b) and 4 figures are off.
risks.mitigation: Landings made by `seed_landed(.., 10.0)` last 10 minutes and start 2 hours apart (hestia.rs:4252-4281); failed jobs start 30 minutes after their slot's landing start and run 5 minutes. Each test asserts `waste_windows` attempt counts per window before asserting results.

risks.risk: Window and retry reconstruction can drift: a landing record written later moves a landing end, and a 'try again on' link can point at a missing job.
risks.mitigation: A missing or unrun predecessor counts as no predecessor; the docs call the figures a reconstruction, as `previous_stage_medians` does.

risks.risk: A new record field makes a newer record unreadable by an older Athena because of deny_unknown_fields.
risks.mitigation: skip_serializing_if keeps the field out until the new code writes it; forward reading by old binaries is already limited for every new field in the crate.

risks.risk: Existing hestia tests fail if one of the rewrites in decision 6 is missed or the slowdown noise condition changes a test.
risks.mitigation: Step 6 lists each test and what it asserts afterwards; all existing slowdown tests seed under 60 landings so the slowdown noise rule leaves them unchanged; `cargo test --locked` runs them all.

risks.risk: Gating the slowdown on noise could silence a real slowdown in a repository with 60+ landings and a noisy median.
risks.mitigation: In the slowdown arm the noise check applies only when `bars.median.noise` is Some; otherwise the code path is the current one and the remark says the noise could not be estimated.

demonstrations.method: A new status.rs test builds in-memory records with the existing helpers `timed_job` (status.rs:3261) and `loaded` (3343): 20 landed jobs (index i starts at hour 2i, 20 minutes long) and 20 failed jobs (`OutcomeState::Failed`). Failed job k starts 30 minutes after landing k starts and runs 5 minutes, so it closes after landing k ends and before landing k+1 ends, inside landing k's window. Each failed job's producer invocation costs 0.50 USD via `invocation(&job, 1, Role::Producer, 0.5)` (status.rs:2443). Landings 1-10 get request text 'try again on <id of failed job k-1>' in the form `reading::retry_reference` accepts, so 10 landings are retries and failed jobs 10-19 are never retried. The test first asserts the window counts (20 landings, 20 unlanded, 40 attempts), then calls `waste_windows(&records, THROUGHPUT_WINDOW)` and `Throughput::compute(&records)`. Further cases: only 20 landed jobs; 7 landed jobs (partial window); and a closed unlanded job with no invocations added to the half-failed fixture, which must not change any count (finding 4).
demonstrations.observes: Window 0 holds 40 attempts; attempts per landing is exactly 2.0; first-attempt share is exactly 0.5; wasted spend is 10.00 USD; `Throughput::compute(..).waste` shows the same figures. The no-failure case gives 1.0, 1.0, 0.0. The 7-landing case reports window 0 with landings == 7 and no previous window. Adding a closed unlanded job with no invocations leaves attempts at 40 and `unlanded_jobs` unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `waste_windows` the test does not compile. With attempts counted as landings only, attempts per landing is 1.0; with no retry link the share is 1.0, so the 2.0 and 0.5 assertions fail. Without the guard inside `did_not_land` the no-invocation job makes attempts 41 and the guard assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `status::waste_windows` (added by step 2) and `Throughput::compute` (exists, status.rs ~984). Fixtures `timed_job`, `loaded`, `invocation` exist (status.rs:3261, 3343, 2443); the test edits request text and invocation cost on the loaded records. No double stands in front of the logic under test.

demonstrations.method: Two tests. (a) Pure `throughput_due(landed, median, waste, latest)` with `earlier_review_with_waste(10, 10.0, Some(attempts 1.5, wasted 2.00, share 0.8))`. Case A: 15 landed, same median 10.0, wasted 2.50, other figures equal returns Some(Wasted). Case C: all figures equal returns None. Case B: wasted 2.50 with no landing since (10 landed) returns None; exactly 2.40 (20%) with 15 landed returns None. Case D: attempts 1.9, then share 0.6, each return Some(Wasted). Case E: previous with `waste: None` returns None. Case F: previous wasted 0.0 and current 0.5 with attempts equal returns None; with attempts up 25% returns Some(Wasted). (b) Review level: 80 landings in four windows (`seed_landed(.., 0, 80, 10.0)`, median flat), failed attempts from `seed_failed` at 1.00 USD each: windows 3, 2, 1, 0 hold 2, 5, 2, 10. The previous review (75 landings, median 10.0, stored wasted 2.00) is stored with `put_earlier_review_with_waste`; 80 - 75 is 5 landings, so cadence does not fire and only the spend rise can. `athena.throughput_review(&Quiet)` runs with `throughput_model(6.0)` injected through `athena_with`. The test asserts `waste_windows` attempt counts per window (22, 25, 22, 30 attempts) and that the median trigger would be None before the review.
demonstrations.observes: (a) The Some/None results above, with the median identical in A and C. (b) The record has trigger `Wasted` and `window_median_minutes` 10.0, and the model log has one entry. Spend rose 10 vs 2 (change 8) against noise 3 and floor 1.00, so the gate queues one design request and the note names wasted spend as beyond noise.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the waste argument and the Wasted branch, Case A returns None because the median is unchanged, and the review-level case returns Ok(None) because nothing is due.
demonstrations.seam: Production `hestia::throughput_due` (signature changed in step 4) and `Athena::throughput_review` (exists, hestia.rs ~1701). Existing fixtures: `athena_with`, `seed_landed`, `put_earlier_review`, `throughput_model` (hestia.rs:4233-4346), `earlier_review` literal (4348). Step 6 adds `earlier_review_with_waste`, `put_earlier_review_with_waste` and `seed_failed(dir, athena, slot, usd)`: a Failed job built with `timed_job` starting 30 minutes after the slot's landing start, producer cost set via `invocation(..).cost`, committed with `put`. `seed_landed(.., 10.0)` landings last 10 minutes and the next starts 2 hours later (4252-4281), so each failed job closes inside its slot's window. Noise comes from the real `Throughput::compute`.

demonstrations.method: A new hestia.rs test: `athena_with`, `seed_landed(.., 0, 10, 25.0)`, `put_earlier_review_citing` (previous review whose proposal's `request_job` is the open request), `open_design_request_job` (id 20260905-000000-d000), then `seed_stages(.., 10, 11, slow_stages())` so the median rises 25 to 60 over 21 landings. The fake `throughput_model(6.0)` logs each THROUGHPUT.md it receives. It calls `athena.throughput_review(&Quiet)`.
demonstrations.observes: The review returns a record whose note contains the open request's id, 'still open', 'design request: not enough history: 21 of 60 landings, none queued', and, for the slowdown, 'noise could not be estimated' with 'slowdown request ... queued at high priority'. The note therefore agrees with what happened: no design request was queued (open_design_requests stays 1, proposal is Some with `request_job == None`), the slowdown request was queued under the unchanged 25% rule because 21 landings give no noise estimate. The model log has exactly one entry and that THROUGHPUT.md names d000.

demonstrations.method: Four tests. (a) Pure `request_gate` over in-memory window figures: change 0.1 attempts against noise 0.3 gives queue false and a note containing 'within noise'; change 0.5 against 0.3 gives queue true, naming measure, change, noise, floor and 'differences'; change equal to the bar is within; a share that fell counts as worse; an improved or unmoved measure gives 'no measure worsened'; flat-history cases: older windows flat (noise 0) and window 0 worse by exactly one job (attempts per landing +0.05, share -0.05, or spend +one attempt's median cost) gives queue false with 'within noise'; two jobs' worth gives queue true; a median up by 0.5 minute over flat windows is within, up by 2 minutes beyond; under 60 landings gives queue false with 'not enough history: N of 60'; the same with no earlier review and no open request gives queue true, and with an open request false. (b) Review level on the criterion 2(b) fixture (80 landings, flat median, 1.00 USD failed attempts, windows 3/2/1 hold 2/5/2, so spend noise 3 USD, attempts noise 0.15, share and median noise 0, floors 0.05 and 1 minute) with the previous review at 75 landings citing the open d000 and a stored baseline of 2.00. Within case: window 0 holds 4 failed (spend +2, attempts +0.1) and the stored baseline 2.00 makes `Wasted` fire (asserted before the note). Beyond case: window 0 holds 10 failed (spend +8, attempts +0.4); also asserts two design requests are open and `improvement_of` lists both. (c) Clean-history case (finding 2): windows 1-3 hold 0 failed, window 0 exactly one failed run, stored baseline 0.0, previous review placed at 70 landings so 80 - 70 = 10 makes the Cadence trigger fire; the test asserts the record's trigger is `Cadence` before asserting the note. (d) Slowdown within noise: 80 landings whose window medians are 10, 22, 10, 22 minutes (noise 12), the previous review stored at median 10 with 75 landings and a window-0 median of 14 (rise 4, over 25% and a stage grew via `seed_stages`), asserting no slowdown request is queued and the note says 'slowdown request: ... within noise'; a second case with flat older windows and a 14 minute median queues the slowdown request.
demonstrations.observes: Within (b): trigger Wasted, model log one entry, proposal `request_job None`, only d000 open, note contains 'within noise', 'still open' and the difference count (2). Beyond (b): one model call, a second design request queued, `improvement_of` lists d000 and the new one, note names spend and attempts as beyond noise. (c): trigger Cadence, nothing queued, note 'within noise'. (d): within-noise slowdown queues none; flat-history slowdown queues one. Pure cases give the results above.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the gate, the within-noise case still queues a request, so 'only d000 open' and the 'within noise' note fail. Without the floor, the flat-history cases (noise 0, change 0.05) queue and fail. Without the slowdown noise condition, case (d) queues a slowdown request.
demonstrations.seam: Production `hestia::request_gate`, `hestia::slowdown_beyond_noise` (pure, step 4) and `Athena::throughput_review` (step 5). Fixtures: in-memory values for (a); for (b)-(d) the seed helpers, `seed_failed`, `seed_stages`, `put_earlier_review_with_waste`, `put_earlier_review_citing` (step 6) and the fake driver injected by `athena_with`. Window figures, noise and floors come from the real `Throughput::compute`, not from a double.

open_questions: User: When an earlier design request is still open and the change is beyond noise, should a second design request be queued (this plan does, and tells the model about the open one), or should the review record the proposal and queue nothing until the open request closes?

User: Below 60 landings the noise cannot be estimated. This plan queues no design request then (except the very first review) and lets the existing 25% slowdown rule alone decide the slowdown request. Should it instead queue on any worsening, or should the slowdown request also wait for 60 landings?

User: This plan asks the model on every due review, as it does today when no request is open, so a due review costs one model call even when no request is queued. Should a review whose change is within noise skip the model to save that cost?

User: The floors are one job's worth (1/20 for attempts per landing and first-attempt share, the median cost of one did-not-land attempt for spend) and 1 minute for the median. Is one minute the right smallest change in the median that counts?
